title: Sculpture & 3D: Application
welcome_lead: Apply ideas from Moore, Hepworth and modern installation.
meta_desc: Applying GCSE sculpture: Henry Moore, Barbara Hepworth, installation artists.
final_note: These artists turned 3D form into emotional language.

concepts.def: Hole through a sculpture, used by Hepworth.

walkthroughs.body_html: Henry Moore (1898-1986) made reclining figures in bronze and stone. He believed in truth to materials — letting wood look like wood, stone like stone — and used hollowed-out spaces so air became part of the form.

Barbara Hepworth (1903-1975) led direct carving and was the first to pierce a sculpture all the way through in 1931. Her smooth abstract forms in wood and stone explore the relationship between mass and void.

Cornelia Parker creates installation works using found objects. Cold Dark Matter: An Exploded View (1991) suspended the fragments of a literally exploded garden shed, lit so its shadows became part of the work — a sculpture made of charcoal and light.
